title: Olmec centre at San Lorenzo
description: The earliest major Olmec centre flourishes, known for its colossal stone heads.

title: Teotihuacan at its height
description: The city of the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon holds more than 100,000 people, among the largest in the world at the time.

title: Death of Pakal the Great
description: The Maya king of Palenque dies after a reign of 68 years and is buried under the Temple of the Inscriptions.

title: Tenochtitlan founded
description: The Mexica settle on an island in Lake Texcoco, where their capital grows into one of the largest cities in the world.

title: Triple Alliance formed
description: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan ally to overthrow Azcapotzalco, the beginning of the Aztec Empire.

title: Cortés meets Moctezuma
description: Hernán Cortés and his Spanish and Tlaxcalan force enter Tenochtitlan and are received by the emperor.

title: Fall of Tenochtitlan
description: After a siege of nearly three months, with smallpox raging in the city, the Spaniards and their native allies capture it.

title: Viceroyalty of New Spain established
description: Antonio de Mendoza arrives as the first viceroy of a territory that comes to stretch from Central America to California.

title: Silver found at Zacatecas
description: The discovery starts one of the richest silver mining districts of the Spanish Empire.

title: Cry of Dolores
description: The priest Miguel Hidalgo calls his parishioners to revolt, starting the War of Independence.

title: Independence won
description: The Army of the Three Guarantees under Agustín de Iturbide enters Mexico City, ending Spanish rule.

title: Battle of San Jacinto
description: Texan rebels defeat and capture Santa Anna, and Texas becomes independent of Mexico.

title: American army takes Mexico City
description: The fall of the capital decides the Mexican–American War, which costs Mexico about half its territory.

title: Constitution of 1857
description: A liberal constitution limits the power of the Church and the army, and civil war follows.

title: Battle of Puebla
description: Mexican troops defeat an invading French army, the victory remembered on Cinco de Mayo.

title: Execution of Maximilian
description: The Austrian archduke installed as emperor by France is shot, and Benito Juárez restores the republic.

title: Porfirio Díaz takes power
description: Díaz overthrows the government and dominates Mexico for 35 years of order, foreign investment and growing inequality.

title: Mexican Revolution begins
place: San Luis Potosí (the date named in Madero's plan)
description: Francisco Madero's call to rise against Díaz starts a decade of revolution and civil war.

title: Constitution of 1917
description: The constitution still in force sets out land reform, labour rights and national ownership of what lies under the soil.

title: Zapata killed
description: The peasant leader Emiliano Zapata is ambushed by government troops.

title: Oil industry nationalised
description: President Lázaro Cárdenas expropriates the foreign oil companies.

title: Tlatelolco massacre
place: Plaza de las Tres Culturas, Mexico City
description: Soldiers fire on a student demonstration ten days before the Olympic Games open in the city.

title: Mexico City earthquake
description: An earthquake of magnitude 8.0 kills at least 5,000 people in the capital.

title: Zapatista uprising
place: San Cristóbal de las Casas, Chiapas
description: Indigenous rebels take towns in Chiapas on the day the North American Free Trade Agreement comes into force.

title: End of one-party rule
description: Vicente Fox wins the presidency, the first defeat for the Institutional Revolutionary Party in 71 years.
